A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VC-Inspector work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, human explanation ratings, caption-refinement experiments, and computational measurements, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds human-rated YouCook2 evaluation, hallucination-detection results, and a caption-refinement case study.

M1.justification: The object/action corruption pipeline, deterministic training scores, Qwen2.5-VL backbones, LoRA training, frozen visual components, and joint score/explanation outputs remain unchanged. Prompt corrections and rewritten descriptions do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds human-rated YouCook2-Eval with model-generated, mismatched, and ground-truth captions, extending beyond the retained synthetic YouCook2-FG-Eval scenario. It also adds FOIL-COCO and ActivityNet-FOIL single-object hallucination-detection tasks. Existing training and evaluation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The retained Flickr8K comparison expands substantially: v3 Table 4 adds FLEUR, HICE-S, and PAC-S++ with ViT-B/ViT-L configurations in both reference settings, plus Polos in the reference-based setting. These are new reported comparator rows, although several methods were already cited in v2. VATEX comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The explanation study changes from 100 captions rated by three authors to 50 captions rated by two evaluators, introducing mismatched explanation-caption controls for half the evaluation data and normalized, discounted scoring. New protocols include 20 YouCook2 videos with five captions each rated by three annotators, and FOIL classification accuracy. Existing training settings and the VATEX subset remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds controlled single-object-error sensitivity tests, mismatched-explanation controls addressing rating bias, and a five-round CAPability refinement case study in Appendix B.2/Figure 7. Existing object/action and explanation-supervision ablations, full CAPability results, and computational analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v2 reports a standard deviation and ordinal Krippendorff’s alpha for human explanation ratings. v3 removes both, retaining within-one-point evaluator agreement alongside its redesigned score. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty or confidence intervals for the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: v3 adds YouCook2-Eval results of 72.8/80.3 for VC-Inspector-7B Kendall/Spearman correlation, FOIL accuracies of 99.6/99.3 for VC-Inspector-3B, and additional Flickr8K comparator scores. In Table 2, BLEU_4 Spearman values change from 36.28/29.56 to 14.81/25.60, and PAC-S Kendall values from 32.60/31.40 to 31.40/38.10, for one/nine references. The explanation study replaces its 4.33 mean rating with a noncomparable controlled score of 0.62. Figure 7 newly reports refinement from 3/5 to 5/5. Retained VC-Inspector benchmark scores otherwise match up to rounding.

T1.justification: v3 Section 4.7 introduces a mathematical definition for the controlled explanation score: normalized correct-pair score multiplied by one minus the incorrect-pair score. The original data-generation scoring mathematics remains unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: controllable factual-error synthesis, an interpretable reference-free evaluator, strong human correlation and generalization, and useful caption-refinement feedback. The additional benchmarks primarily supply evidence for these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets FOIL performance as evidence of sensitivity to targeted object hallucinations and explicitly discusses potential high-rating bias in explanation assessment. Figure 7 adds interpretations of specific refinement corrections. The limitations concerning unmodeled attributes/relations, synthetic supervision, and computational costs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.5 repairs the malformed substitution placeholder and standardizes the input variable from {{cap}} to {{caption}}, improving the documented prompt template. v3 also identifies UMBC HPCF as an experimental computing resource. Training hyperparameters and project access information remain equivalent.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for FOIL, Gemini 2.5, PDVC, and PAC-S++. The principal positioning against embedding-based and proprietary evaluators remains stable. Numerous year/venue updates and consolidation of duplicate CLAIR entries concern existing works rather than new research positioning.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: baselines receive a subsection, synthetic consistency and human correlation are separated, dataset descriptions move into their corresponding experiments, and computational efficiency moves from Appendix B.1 to Section 4.8. The introduction’s evaluation overview is rewritten, with additional terminology, grammar, and bibliographic editing.

P2.justification: v3 adds separate YouCook2 and FOIL tables, substantially expands the Flickr8K comparison table, and introduces a full-page refinement visualization with timestamps and highlighted caption changes in Figure 7. Existing Figures 1–6 and appendix tables are retained, with relocations and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through direct hallucination-sensitivity tests, additional human-rated captions, and broader Flickr8K comparisons. These gains are tempered by the small added human benchmark and an explanation study with fewer examples and raters and less statistical reporting, despite its useful mismatch control. Overall, the revision provides a limited net improvement over v2’s already extensive validation.
